'''The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game''' (LOTR TCG) was a card game by Decipher, Inc. based on Peter Jackson's ''Lord of the Rings'' films. Decipher also published the [[Star Wars CCG]]. The game ran from 2001 to 2007, and fans have kept it going since then.<ref name="pcdec">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher], LOTR-TCG Wiki (Player's Council). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008212029/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Internet Archive]</ref> Unique cards print a uniqueness dot (•) before the title; non-unique cards do not.<ref name="lotr-unique">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Unique Unique], LOTR-TCG Wiki. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230320120113/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/unique Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="lotr-cr42">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Comprehensive_Rules_4.2 Comprehensive Rules 4.2], LOTR-TCG Wiki, unique and non-unique. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20251228160932/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Comprehensive_Rules_4.2 Internet Archive]</ref>

== History ==
Decipher announced in August 2000 that it had the film license. The first set, ''The Fellowship of the Ring'', came out in November 2001, one month before the film. Decipher then released a set about every four months.<ref name="pcdec" /> In late 2001 Decipher lost the Star Wars license to Wizards of the Coast (see [[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]), so LOTR became its main game.<ref name="pcdec" />

''Shadows'' (2004) was a partial reboot. It was unpopular with fans, and the game began a long decline. Staff cuts delayed later sets. ''The Wraith Collection'' was put out to buy time before ''The Hunters''. The last sets were made by a single employee, and the final set, ''Age's End'', was printed right up until Decipher's license expired.<ref name="pcdec" />

Later online championships on GEMP were run by the Player's Council.<ref name="pcwc" />

== Fan continuation ==
The fan forums and card wiki were hosted at lotrtcgwiki.com (The Last Homely House).<ref name="t5072a" /> In June 2020 fans formed the Player's Council, which runs the GEMP online client, new "V" sets, errata and leagues, much like the SWCCG [[Players Committee]].<ref name="pcpc">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Player%27s_Council Player's Council], LOTR-TCG Wiki. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260208110434/https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Player%27s_Council Internet Archive]</ref>

== SWCCG players in LOTR TCG ==
The 2010 LOTR World Championship was a free Movie Block event on Friday 13 August 2010 at the Philadelphia Airport Hilton, during SWCCG Worlds. James Barnes was the tournament director and [[Chris Schoenthal]] was the backup for rulings.<ref name="t5072a">[https://lotrtcgwiki.com/forums/index.php?topic=5072.0 LOTR Worlds Event 2010], CategoryOneGames.com (18 June 2010), The Last Homely House forums. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20241225194037/https://lotrtcgwiki.com/forums/index.php?PHPSESSID=1d97lua1cs98duriomvsvv6ko2&topic=5072.0%3Bprev_next=prev Internet Archive]</ref> The event was run by the SWCCG Players Committee.<ref name="pcwc" /> One poster said its 16 players were "riding the coat tails of SW".<ref name="t5072c">[https://lotrtcgwiki.com/forums/index.php?topic=5072.30 LOTR Worlds Event 2010, page 3], The Last Homely House forums (final standings posted 22 September 2010). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260519222258/https://lotrtcgwiki.com/forums/index.php?topic=5072.30 Internet Archive]</ref>
